name: Aretha Franklin
hook: A Detroit preacher's daughter whose first label never knew what to do with her gospel voice, and whose second sent her to Muscle Shoals to use it, which produced 'Respect'.
blurb: Aretha Franklin was born in Memphis on 25 March 1942 and grew up in Detroit, where her father, C. L. Franklin, was pastor of New Bethel Baptist Church and a famous preacher across the country. She sang gospel in his church as a girl, and singers like Ray Charles and Sam Cooke visited the family home. Columbia signed her in 1960, at 18, and spent six years having her sing jazz, old standards and blues without finding her a hit; John Hammond later said the label did not understand her gospel background. In November 1966 the producer Jerry Wexler signed her to Atlantic with the opposite plan, to build the records around her gospel singing and piano. In January 1967 he took her to Rick Hall's FAME studio in Muscle Shoals, Alabama, to record with its band. That session produced 'I Never Loved a Man (The Way I Love You)' and ended after one day in a fight involving Hall and her then husband and manager, Ted White, so the work moved to New York with the Muscle Shoals players flown in. In April 1967 her version of Otis Redding's 'Respect', rewritten from a man's demand into hers, became a number one hit and an anthem for the civil rights and women's movements. 'Amazing Grace', recorded in January 1972, took her back to church. In 1987 she became the first woman in the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. She died in Detroit on 16 August 2018.

signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The one song finished at Muscle Shoals before the session fell apart: gospel piano and a Southern rhythm section.

signatureTracks.title: Respect
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Otis Redding's song, made hers, and the record that made her a star.

signatureTracks.title: Bridge over Troubled Water
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Paul Simon's gospel-inspired song taken back into church. Simon called it his favourite cover of anything he wrote.
